A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLoT research work. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, equations and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original RLoT benchmark results, cross-model and cross-task transfer experiments, navigator ablations and reasoning-cost measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original RLoT experiments and adds self-evaluation validation, latency measurements, baseline comparisons and component analyses.

M1.justification: The main five-block navigator, state representation, DQN training and prompts remain unchanged. Appendix I introduces evaluated extensions adding Follow-up-question, Rephrasing or Compression blocks to the action space, constituting limited procedural variants.

E1.justification: The seven principal benchmarks and their mathematics, STEM and commonsense tasks remain covered. New analyses examine existing reasoning states and method components. Omitted MATH-500 columns concern subset-level reporting within retained mathematical-task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 9 adds rStar, AFlow and DSPy to the extended comparison. Tables 13–14 add a finetuned LLM navigator and repeated Refine/Debate controls. The LLM-as-navigator comparator is removed from the corresponding PRM comparison. Refine/Self-Refine and MCTS/Basic MCTS are matched renamings.

E3.justification: Existing shared hyperparameters remain unchanged. New evaluation designs include manual checking of 100 intermediate states, per-problem timing, Gaussian reward perturbations with standard deviation 0.1, alternative navigator architectures and retraining with individual blocks removed. These substantially expand the experimental controls and procedures.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's illustrative state example and basic navigator/ORM comparisons, v2 adds a self-evaluation audit, repeated-block controls, degraded/stronger PRM tests, block-removal ablations and additional-block experiments. The original learning curves, reasoning case study and block-analysis figures are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix C/Table 7 newly reports solving-time means and standard deviations across three repeats. v1 provides no corresponding repeated-run variability estimates. This addition concerns latency; uncertainty reporting for benchmark accuracy remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises the DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B results: RLoT's reported average changes from 71.05 to 82.92 and AIME24 from 33.33 to 63.33. The cause of these revisions is unspecified; other model rows and transfer results remain unchanged. v2 also adds latency, comparator and diagnostic results, while removing MATH-500 entries from the navigator and reward comparisons.

T1.justification: The MDP definitions, autoregressive likelihood and discounted-return expressions remain equivalent. Appendix J restates the existing framework and pipeline without introducing a substantive mathematical definition, theorem, proof or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same adaptive-reasoning contribution, reported advantage of up to 13.4%, navigator with fewer than 3K parameters, model-size efficiency and transferability claims. Added appendix evidence does not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Appendices F–I add substantive interpretations of structured self-evaluation, alternative navigator complexity, PRM robustness and generalization, and the benefits or failures of additional blocks. Conversely, v1 Appendix H.1's explicit limitation concerning precise numerical computation and its proposed tool-based remedy disappear, along with the broader-impact discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix J adds hard-question selection prompts, the reference model and sample counts, a detailed training/inference walkthrough, and SymPy-based answer equivalence with random selection when no majority exists. Appendix G discloses 20K samples for the supervised navigator. These substantially expand documentation; the original hyperparameters, action prompts and code-access information remain.

R1.justification: Section 5.1 now distinguishes fixed workflows from adaptive search methods and emphasizes avoiding search costs. Targeted citations are added for automated workflows, self-correction, cognition and PRM quality, while the reinforcement-fine-tuning discussion and its two sources are removed. The broader inference-time/RL positioning persists.

P1.justification: The appendices are extensively reordered and divided into dedicated analyses, with implementation details moved into an expanded pipeline explanation. v2 adds Section 4.6, rewrites related-work passages, moves ethics into the main text and adds reproducibility and LLM-use statements. Much of the original main narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds tables for latency, score/token comparisons, navigator alternatives, PRM quality, block ablations/extensions and training-data statistics. Existing comparison tables gain rows or lose columns. All five original figure artworks are retained, but several displays are relocated or resized, alongside document-wide typography and header changes.

improvement.justification: New state-validation, block-removal and PRM-robustness evidence, broader workflow comparisons and fuller implementation details improve support and reproducibility. However, v2 removes the numerical-precision limitation and leaves unexplained DeepSeek score revisions. Tables 14–15 also retain four-task averages after removing MATH-500: RLoT remains 73.34 although the displayed three-task mean is 72.18. These reporting weaknesses temper the overall gain.
